chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

If I were to strike the nose of a believer with this sword of mine on condition that he would hate me, he would not hate me; and if I were to pour out the world with all its wealth before a hypocrite on condition that he would love me, he would not love me.

And that is because it was decreed and concluded upon the tongue of the Unlettered Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he said: 'O Ali, a believer will not hate you and a hypocrite will not love you.'

key_terms.خَيْشُومَ: the nose (often used metonymically for the person or face)

ai.seo_question: Why do believers love Imam Ali and hypocrites hate him according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) illustrates the metaphysical bond of *wilayah* by asserting that the love of true believers and the hatred of hypocrites are fixed by divine decree (*qada'*), transcending worldly incentives. This concept is rooted in the Prophet’s declaration to Ali that his status as the locus of divine love ensures believers naturally gravitate toward him while hypocrites are inherently repelled, a principle deeply cherished in Shia theology as evidence of spiritual authenticity.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 45. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:

Even if I strike the nose of a believer with this, my sword, for hating me he will not hate me, and even if I pile all the wealth of the world before a hypocrite (Muslim) for loving me he will not love me.

This is because it is a verdict pronounced by the tongue of the revered Prophet, may Allāh bless him and his descendants, as he said: “O ‘Alī, a believer will never hate you and a hypocrite will never love you.” [1]
